name: run
note: (anim-rework S2, real-world standard, keyed by hand; never traced; M6) The standing holstered run at full speed (4 m/s): a controlled operator run, not a sprint, with the forward lean it had before (pelvis 12, chest 18 deg: M6 "similar to the lean it has now"), the head up; feet landing close to the line under the hips (legs add 3 deg: about 4 cm a foot), knees forward over the toes (the knee pole a touch inward, kneeOut -0.045), a higher back kick and knee drive; the upper arms swinging from the shoulder along the sides (in the world about 25 back to 35 forward), elbows 85-95 deg close to the ribs (abd 4), hands from behind the hip to chest height, toward but never across the midline. Duty and swing lift match the planner's run. Angles in degrees in the body frame (x right, y up, z forward): pitch about x (+ the top forward), yaw about y (+ turns right), roll about z (+ the right side up). Pelvis offsets in cm from rest (the height adds to the legs' own reach drop). Arms: flex (+ forward, in the chest frame: the world angle is flex minus the chest pitch), abd (+ out), elbow (+ bent), inward (the forearm turned in toward the midline). Legs (the Blender preview and the track only: the game's feet come from the foot planner): flex (+ the knee forward), add (+ the foot in toward the midline), knee (+ bent), ankle (+ the toes up). Phase 0 is the left foot strike; keys 0-0.375 are mirrored. (anim-rework S2b) The back swing reaches -45 deg in the world (flex -27 in the 18 deg chest) so the hands pass the hip; the trunk counter-rotates (pelvis yaw 3 as slice 2, chest -8: the chest carries the counter-rotation; the review asked pelvis yaw 7, which read the forward foot off the line in the pelvis frame (e2e-anim track <= 7 cm), and pelvis 4 put the knees 3.5 cm outside the ankles). Trunk angles are absolute in the body frame (key_clip.py fk), so the chest lean is 18 deg, not the pelvis + spine + chest sum.
